basis: Original PNG pixels opened once in fresh image context, before reading candidate geometry or candidate source inventory.

groups.sourceFact: One unframed perspective apparatus, not a set of subfigures. There is no coordinate grid, data table, measured scale, dimension, numeric given, or labelled mathematical point.

A tall U-shaped/horseshoe magnet dominates the image. Two long limbs are joined by the curved upper return; their lower pole regions flank the working region. Perspective outlines and dark shading distinguish the limbs and pole faces.

The right lower pole carries a legible N. A light glyph on the dark left lower region is degraded and cannot be independently transcribed confidently. No unsupported S or other pole designation is licensed.

A compact rectangular/parallelogram multi-turn wire coil lies in the lower magnet pole-gap region, with visible roughly parallel winding traces and depth. The scan supports several turns, not a reliable exact winding integer.
A shaft/axle projects diagonally toward the lower left from the coil region; the coil, shaft, and hub/contact region belong to the same apparatus, not detached panels.

A curved directional mark is visible beside the projecting left axle end. It conveys rotation around the shaft; it is not a current arrow or a magnetic-field arrow. No quantitative speed or angle is given.

Two band/curved contact features appear along the shaft near its projecting end, with pickup/contact strokes and two distinct flexible leads hanging down-left into free ends. The visible contact and lead relationships must remain; the scan does not establish continuity, segmentation, insulation, hidden terminals, or a slip-ring/split-ring classification.
